sections.h2: What can the Williamston registrar's office do for me?
sections.html:
Look for it on the ground-level floor of the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston, where its own page says the land records start in 1771. Easements, agreements, assignments, releases, plats, deeds and deeds of trust are all recorded at this counter, and an index tracks them, with a separate index for plats.

Uniform commercial code statements join the real estate books too, a practice the county dates to July 1, 2001. Other jobs include filing military discharge papers (DD-214), keeping assumed business name, partnership and incorporation instruments, and giving oaths to notaries. Vital records on hand begin in October 1913 for births and deaths and in 1883 for marriage licenses, with an index for 1872 to 1882.

A seller should remember that whatever sits in these books is what a title searcher will find. Look first.

sections.h2: Can Martin County deeds be searched online?
sections.html:
Yes: the county points to martinrod.org for deeds, with records back to 1771. A separate online service takes vital record orders, and an index of births, deaths and marriages is posted too.

An hour in the index pays off for a house you inherited or have held for decades.

  • Search under your name and under the previous owner's name.
  • Match the legal description on the latest deed to the tax record.
  • Watch for old deeds of trust with no release after them.
  • Note any plat or state right of way plan that touches the lot.

sections.h2: What does Martin County list as its recording charges?
sections.html:
The county's fee sheet follows the statewide schedule and warns that amounts may change. Call about the total before you mail a payment, and write money orders to Martin County Register of Deeds.

Charges as listed by Martin County, selected lines
ServiceCharge
Deed or other instrument, pages 1 to 15$26
Pages beyond 15$4 each
Deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64
Plat or map (18 x 24)$21.00 a page
State right of way plans$21.00 first page, $5.00 after
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 after
Uncertified photocopy$0.25 a page
Deed excise tax$2.00 per $1000 of price
Cancellation or satisfactionNo fee
Extra instrument within one document$10.00 each

A re-recorded instrument costs the same as the original unless pages were added, and each added page is $4.

sections.h2: How should a deed be formatted before it goes to Martin County?
sections.html:
Paper signed on or after July 1, 2002 has to meet the layout standard the county quotes from G.S. 161-10. Miss it and the office adds $25.00 to the recording charge.

  • Letter or legal paper, 8 1/2 inches wide.
  • Three inches left blank at the head of page one, with half an inch on the other edges.
  • Black on white, type no smaller than 9 points, printed on one face.
  • Instrument type named at the top of page one.

Blanks and corrections may be inked by hand, and exhibits face the same standard. What counts is the day it was signed, not the day it arrives.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax at a Martin County closing?
sections.html:
The seller. Martin County's sheet gives $2.00 per $1000 of purchase price, and the statute expresses that as $1.00 for each $500 or part of $500.

The register takes it at filing, splitting it between the county general fund and the state. The county may retain 2 percent of the state portion.

The settlement statement prints the dollar amount. No deed gets filed until it is paid, so let the statement settle the number.

sections.h2: Why does filing sequence matter on a Williamston sale?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18 a conveyance, an option, a lease over three years or a right of first refusal gains force over lien creditors and paying purchasers only through registration. Martin County land registers here whatever the owner's address.

If a creditor's judgment is filed ahead of your buyer's deed, the buyer can rank behind it. Attorneys avoid that by filing as soon as funds are confirmed.

  • Mail or deliver the signed deed with any lender release in a single packet.
  • Enclose the recording fee and the excise tax.
  • Get the book and page reference after recording.

sections.h2: What else does the Martin County office issue besides land records?
sections.html:
Marriage licenses and certified vital records are the other daily business, and heirs selling an inherited house often need the second kind. A certified copy of a birth, death or marriage record costs $10.00, and the county limits who may request one: the person named, a spouse, parents, siblings, children, grandchildren or grandparents, an authorized agent or attorney, or someone who needs it for a legal determination of a personal or property right and can prove it.

An executor or heir therefore usually brings proof of the relationship or a document showing legal authority. Uncertified copies are open to the public at $0.25 a page.

  • Marriage license fee: $60.00, issued between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM, valid for 60 days from issue.
  • Both parties must appear with proof of age and proof of a Social Security number.
  • A divorced applicant brings the divorce decree.
  • The county says a premarital physical is no longer required.

sections.h2: When does Martin County send tax bills, and when is interest charged?
sections.html:
A recorded deed leaves the tax bill alone. Bills for real and personal property go out in July or August, with a September 1 due date. Interest-free payment runs through January 5, or the next business day if January 5 lands on a weekend or holiday.

A 2 percent penalty starts January 6, and interest of three-fourths of one percent accrues monthly after that. The collector must also advertise unpaid real estate tax in the local newspaper from March 1 to June 30, and the taxpayer pays extra for that notice.

Visit the collector at 305 East Main Street, Room 125, any weekday from 8 AM to 5 PM, or call 252-789-4360. A payoff quote before closing lets the bill come out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: How does Martin County's housing stock look in Census data?
sections.html:
The mid-2025 estimate is 21,601 people, a 2.0 percent drop from the April 2020 base, living among 11,071 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied rate was 66.8 percent and the median home value $109,700.

Household income at the median was $48,578 in 2024 dollars, and 19.7 percent of people live in poverty. Building permits for 2025 numbered zero. Seniors make up 26.9 percent of the population, and median gross rent is $758.

With values this modest, deferred repairs can make a traditional lender balk. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands and close once title is clear. Have your attorney run the land records early so any deed of trust still uncancelled is released before closing.

faqs.q: Where in Williamston is the Martin County register of deeds?
faqs.a: In the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston, on the first floor. The county prints (252) 789-4320 for record questions.

faqs.q: How old are the Martin County land records?
faqs.a: To 1771. Martin County says the index of recorded instruments starts that year, with deeds searchable at martinrod.org.

faqs.q: What is the Martin County fee for a deed of trust?
faqs.a: $64 through page 35, plus $4 per additional page or fraction. A plain deed costs $26 through page 15.

faqs.q: Does Martin County charge for recording a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. Cancellations, certificates of satisfaction and notices of satisfaction all carry no fee on the county's list.

faqs.q: Who pays Martin County's deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller, at $2.00 per $1000 of price by the county's wording, collected before the deed is recorded.
